mechanism: Trimethoprim inhibits renal tubular secretion of potassium and can increase serum potassium levels, while irbesartan (ARB) also increases potassium retention, creating a synergistic hyperkalemia risk.
action: Monitor serum potassium and renal function regularly; consider potassium-sparing alternative antibiotics if possible, especially in patients with renal impairment or baseline hyperkalemia risk.
